the synthesis of the mRNA for the dopamine receptor D2 is decreased by approximately 50% in the aged rat striatum, and the decrease in the mRNA is correlated with the decrease in the number of D2 receptors.

the effects of aging on the synthesis of the striatal dopamine D2 receptor mRNA.
the role of the dopamine system in aging.
the synthesis of the mRNA for the striatal D2 receptor, and its relation to aging and to dopamine receptor loss.

the decrease in the synthesis rate of the dopamine D1 receptor mRNA is not a primary event in the aging process.

the decrease in striatal D2 mRNA levels during aging is a reflection of a decreased synthetic capacity of the striatal dopamine receptor mRNA, and that this decreased synthetic capacity is a reflection of the aging process itself.
aging is associated with a significant decrease in D2 dopamine receptor gene expression in the rat striatum.

the decrease in dopamine D2 receptors is related to both a loss of cell number and to a decrease in the synthetic capacity of those cells that remain.
the D2 dopamine receptor is the most sensitive of the striatal dopamine receptors to the effects of age.

the age-related decline in dopamine D2 mRNA is not due to cell death.
